subject: Re: Optimizer Toolkit SKU questions and quant/cache guidance
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@deepwave.ai>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Optimizer Toolkit — initial requirements and a couple pricing questions

Hi Hiro,

Thanks for the demo last week — the DeepWave infra team is excited about the latency improvements we saw. Procurement asked me to follow up with a short list of clarifying questions for your sales/finance team around the Optimize Toolkit elements we discussed: batching/caching credits, recommended quantization profiles for our 2B/7B serving mix, and how credits map to SKU tiers. We have an initial usage estimate (~1.2B tokens/month, mixed short/long sessions) and want to model both an annual commit and a pilot.

Could you send a simple SKU-level mapping (pilot vs committed) and the recommended quantization approach for our throughput targets? Also flag any obvious performance vs quality trade-offs we should expect.

Attached: a short requirements doc and sample traffic shape.

Regards,
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Engineering
DeepWave Labs

Attachment: deepwave_requirements_v2.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
From: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@deepwave.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optimizer Toolkit — initial requirements and a couple pricing questions

Samantha — thanks for the note and the traffic file. Short answer: yes, we can present both a pilot SKU and a committed SKU with clear credit mappings; and we have specific quantization recommendations for a mixed 2B/7B fleet. I put a short summary below and attached a first-pass SKU matrix for you to review.

Quick summary (high-level):
- Pilot SKU: fixed monthly credits + burstable compute. Good for smoke testing batching and KV prefix caching.
- Committed SKU: committed tokens/credits with volume tiers; additional efficiency credits for enabling prefix caching + model quantization (4-bit variants where acceptable).
- Quantization guidance: for Llama-family 7B-style models we recommend FP16->4-bit PTQ for inference on dedicated capacity; for 2B models we typically accept dynamic 4-bit quantization with minimal quality loss. If you have high long-context usage, we suggest keeping the 7B at 8-bit hybrid to preserve answer quality.

I've attached sku_matrix_proposal.xlsx. Marissa and Ben — can you take the lead on a pricing sketch and a conservative ops impact note (expected latency change and risk matrix) so we can send a single package to DeepWave by EOD tomorrow?

Best,
Hiro
Head of Sales (APAC coverage)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sku_matrix_proposal.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optimizer Toolkit — initial requirements and a couple pricing questions

Thanks Hiro — taking this on. Ben, I put a few draft numbers in the SKU sheet: pilot = 3-month term, 250M credits/mo baseline, burst to 500M (pay-as-you-go beyond). Committed tiers at 1B, 3B, 6B with progressive per-token pricing and an ops credit that unlocks our suggested KV prefix caching rules (saves ∼18–28% tokens on their shape).

Ops note (short):
- Quantization: 2B -> q4 will reduce latency ~12–18% and cost ~25% in our internal benchmarks. 7B -> q4 gives cost wins but quality regressions on long-context; recommend q8h (8-bit hybrid) for long-session flows or split routing by endpoint.
- Batching: if DeepWave adopts continuous batching with a 20ms coalescing window, we estimate additional 8–12% latency overhead for cold traffic but 30–45% token-cost reduction at scale.
- Guardrails: include a canary phase for any aggressive quant profile (A/B route ~10% traffic).

I'll clean these into the sheet and add a small row for 'expected SLO delta' per SKU. Hiro — want to include a one-time onboarding credit for the pilot to soften procurement asks?

Marissa
Principal Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Hiro / Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement:
1) Procurement asks for the exact mapping between the "ops credit" you mentioned and measurable deliverables (e.g., KV cache configuration applied, expected % token savings, roll-back policy).
2) They want to understand how the quantization choices map to support and rollback — can you document an emergency fallback to 8-bit/FP16 per route?
3) For pilot pricing we need an explicit onboarding credit and an estimate of what metrics will determine success (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, quality guardrails).

I'll share the vendor questionnaire and an initial procurement timeline after our internal review. Can you return a short addendum (1 page) that answers 1–3? That will speed approvals.

—Sam

Hi Samantha / procurement team — Ben here, ops and pricing lead. Attached is the requested 1-page addendum. Highlights:
- Ops credit mapping: we include a one-time ops credit (30 hours of Redwood SRE + configuration labor) for the pilot SKU. Deliverables: KV prefix rules deployed (2 canonical patterns), batching window tuned, and an evaluation run showing token savings. Expected savings: conservative 15% (baseline) to aggressive 28% depending on cache hit characteristics from your traffic file.
- Quantization rollback: for every route we propose a dual-routing canary (10% traffic) and a pre-built fallback to 8-bit hybrid or FP16. Rollback plan: automated traffic split back to baseline model + immediate alerting; typical rollback time < 15 minutes.
- Success metrics (pilot): p95 latency improvement <= +10% vs baseline; cost per 1k tokens <= target band (we put an example in the attached).

We also included a suggested onboarding credit: USD 12,000 for pilot professional services (applied as credits against first two invoices) and a 10% introductory rate reduction on committed tiers if DeepWave signs a 12-month commitment within 45 days of pilot completion.

If that aligns, Hiro / Marissa — can we fold this into a formal commercial sheet and send to Samantha + procurement by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions Pricing
Redwood Inference
